title: UPL SY 10 soybean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: UPL SY 10 soybean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: UPL SY 10 soybean is a grain soybean variety for Mindanao. About 89 days to harvest, 2.1 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: UPL SY 10 soybean is a grain soybean variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 1996 as NSIC 1996 Sy 04. IPB, UPLB CA, College, Laguna bred it. It takes about 89 days from sowing to harvest, with 2.06 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

**Yield:** 2.06 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.
**Recommended for:** Mindanao, in the wet season.

blocks.text: Key facts about UPL SY 10 soybean
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

UPL SY 10 soybean takes about 89 days from sowing to harvest. That is 4.4 days longer than the average of the 19 grain soybean varieties with a day count, 84.6 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 2.06 t/ha beats the average of its group, 1.92. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit soybean fields most often: [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant UPL SY 10 soybean

The registry recommends it for Mindanao in the wet season. Grain soybean goes to feed and food processors, while vegetable soybean, or edamame, is picked green. Pick a variety rated against rust, the main soybean disease here.
